statement: The system shall map each servlet request to the `HttpExchange` values the core expects — `methodToken`, the raw `getRequestURI()` with the context path and the url-pattern prefix the initializer registered stripped at a segment boundary and kept percent-encoded, the raw `getQueryString()`, `getProtocol()`, every header value with duplicates kept and per-name order preserved, `getRemoteAddr()`, `isSecure()` and `getInputStream()` — so that routes, middleware, `Request`, `Response` and `Cookie` behave as on the embedded engine.
acceptanceCriteria: With context path `/app` and pattern `/api/*`, a request to `/app/api/users/%41;v=1?x=%20` reaches a route `/users/:id` with `req.rawPath()` equal to `/users/%41;v=1`, `req.param("id")` equal to `A;v=1` and `req.query("x")` equal to a space; with pattern `/*` or `/` the same request without `/api` reaches the same route, and a request to the bare servlet root reaches the route `/` (empty remainder is `/`). [D-363; D-399]

A request whose raw URI does not start with the context path plus the registered prefix at a segment boundary (a test sends `/app/%61pi/users` to pattern `/api/*`) is answered `404` with the standard error body and a request id, and `getServletPath()`, `getPathInfo()` and `getParameter*` are never read, which a recording `HttpServletRequest` proxy asserts. [D-363; r3 W2-004]

Headers reach `req.header(name)` and `req.headers(name)` with repeated names kept in their per-name order (the Servlet API gives no cross-name order), `Cookie` request headers reach the core cookie parser unchanged (`req.cookie("s")` returns a NaruServe `Cookie`, never `javax.servlet.http.Cookie`), `req.remoteAddress()` is `getRemoteAddr()` and `req.isSecure()` is `isSecure()`; `app.trustProxy(true)` takes effect in the core (FR-ENGINE-008). [D-360]

A shared case suite — route parameters, query decoding, JSON body and `res.json`, cookies read and written, `404`, `405` with `Allow`, automatic `HEAD` and `OPTIONS`, middleware order, `onError` and the standard error body, `res.file` — runs on the Servlet adapter and on the in-memory adapter with identical statuses and bodies, using the same app definition code, so application code needs no change between engines. [D-360; I-021]

The path-rejection cases of D-052 (malformed percent-encoding, invalid UTF-8, an encoded `/`, an encoded or raw `NUL`, `.` and `..` segments raw and encoded) sent as raw request lines to the embedded container are answered `400`, or `404` when the container normalises the path and never reaches the servlet, and never `2xx`; the `OPTIONS *` request is sent too, and the observed status of every case is recorded in `docs/api/servlet.md`. [D-052; I-021]
Header values the framework writes never contain CR or LF on this adapter, and security-related log lines of the adapter carry no token, session id or file content. [I-016; I-017]

statement: The system shall write each response through the container's `HttpServletResponse` — `commit` sets the status with `setStatus` and writes each header with `addHeader` in the given order, and `Content-Length` with `setHeader` exactly as the core gave it, without `sendError`, never adds, removes or changes `Content-Length`, and returns the container's output stream; `finish` completes the response; `abort` marks the exchange aborted so that every later write, `commit` or `finish` throws `IOException`; `sendFile` writes exactly `length` bytes of the file from `offset` in bounded chunks; and a second start of the same exchange throws `IllegalStateException`.
rationale: Covers D-360 (the `Response` behaviour is the core's; the adapter must not alter it), wave decision Servlet adapter semantics left open (r2 W2-006: `abort()` marks the exchange aborted and later writes throw `IOException` because the container owns the socket; response header order is the container's) and the SPI contract of `HttpExchange.commit`, `abort` (idempotent, thread-safe) and `sendFile`. Measured: `spi/HttpExchange.java:55-75` states that the adapter never adds, removes or changes `Content-Length`, that header chars are at most U+00FF and never CR or LF, and that `abort()` may run on any thread while another thread is writing. Decision: header values are written with `addHeader` as given and the `Content-Length` header the core provides with `setHeader` (one rule, no `setContentLength`); the status is set with `setStatus` so the container renders no error page; `abort` does not close the container's socket (the container owns it) and does not call `sendError`; `sendFile` uses `java.io` only (no `java.nio.file`, CON-HTTP-002) and a buffer of at most 64 KiB. Pitfall: `HttpServletResponse.setContentLength` and containers that compute a length for small bodies can change `Content-Length`; the core's header is passed through `setHeader`, and a HEAD response keeps the length the GET body would have had (FR-HTTP-017). Rejected alternative: closing the connection from `abort` through container-specific APIs; it is not portable across containers.

acceptanceCriteria: A reflection test over the main jar named by `naruserve.apiJar` finds every interface declared in `com.snoworca.naruserve`, `.spi` or `.routing` that is the parameter type of a public method of those packages and has exactly one abstract method (ignoring `Object` methods and `default` methods) and fails, naming it, when it lacks `@FunctionalInterface`. [D-350; I-007]
The same test fails, naming the interface, when an interface that is a callback parameter type has no abstract method or more than one, which would stop Kotlin SAM conversion. [D-350]

A Kotlin test passes a lambda to each callback parameter of the matrix: `app.get`/`post`/`route` with `RouteHandler`, `app.use(path) { req, res, next -> }` with `Middleware`, `app.onError`, `app.onStart`, `app.onStop`, `app.server`, `app.multipart`, `app.webSocket`, `app.sse`, `app.ws`, `ws.onText`, `ws.onClose { code, reason -> }` and `res.sse().onClose { }`, each without a receiver DSL, and runs a request or session through the in-memory harness that reaches the lambda; the matrix covers every interface of the AC-1 inventory (16 on 2026-10-20, including the `WebSocketSession` listener types and the SPI types `ExchangeHandler`, `ErrorRenderer`, `StreamDrain` and `UpgradeHandler`, which the test implements as Kotlin lambdas). [D-350; T11]

A second Kotlin test fails the build when the Java reflection inventory of AC-1 names an interface that the Kotlin matrix of AC-3 does not list, by reading the Kotlin matrix from a `CALLBACK_TYPES` list in one shared test class that the Java inventory test compares with its reflection result, so the matrix cannot fall behind the API. [D-350; I-010]

rationale: Covers D-349, the Kotlin part of I-009 and I-010; supports T11. Measured (2026-10-20): `docs/api/*.md` holds 45 ```kotlin blocks (`kotlin.md` 10, `websocket.md` 7, `sse.md` 5, `app.md`, `middleware.md`, `response.md` and `routing.md` 3 each, `json.md` and `request.md` 2 each, `cookie.md`, `express-migration.md`, `logging.md`, `multipart.md`, `static.md`, `README.md` and `lifecycle.md` 1 each); waves 5 and 7 already compile subsets in `JsonDocsKotlinTest`, `SseDocsKotlinTest` and `WebSocketDocsKotlinTest`. Decision: each block is matched by a marker comment `// docs-example: <file>#<n>` (n counts the kotlin blocks of that file from 1) placed before its test function in `NaruServe-api/src/test/kotlin`, `NaruServe-kotlin/src/test/kotlin` or `NaruServe-servlet/src/test/kotlin`; a function holds every non-blank line of its block after whitespace normalisation, or carries `// adapted: <reason>` where it declares an app-defined type, swaps `RestApp.create()` for the in-memory harness replaces `listen`, or is the definition block of the `body()` extension itself, which `NaruServe-kotlin` tests as the module code. Pitfall: matching by block text alone breaks on every doc edit; the position marker fails loudly when a block is inserted before another. Rejected alternative: extracting and compiling the blocks automatically; the blocks are fragments that need app-defined types and an engine-free harness, which the Java docs compile test of OPS-HTTP-004 already solves with a named skip list, and an unrunnable skip is not allowed for D-349.

Restates OPS-HTTP-007 AC-1 to AC-7 and AC-9 unchanged and changes AC-8 (D-380; wave decision Markers pinned by earlier tests, r4 W2-001). Frozen: D-380 says every (미확정) marker of docs/api is resolved or rewritten as a post-v1 item. Deviation (recorded): the three express-migration rows (express.Router(), res.redirect(url), cors()) keep their text because verified assertions pin them (AppDocsTest KEPT via OPS-APP-005 AC-6, WaveFiveDocsTest.kept, HttpDocsTest AC-8 prefix list), so the D-380 check allows exactly those three. Measured (2026-10-20): docs/api/response.md:141 holds the res.redirect marker that OPS-HTTP-007 AC-8 pinned as the only marker line of response.md; wave 8 rewrites it as a post-v1 sentence, which is the one verified assertion that changes. Tests to re-point to OPS-HTTP-008: every HttpDocsTest method that cites OPS-HTTP-007 (AC1 to AC9) and the citation at src/test/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/docs/DocsExamplesCompileTest.java:651-654; the AC8 method sdsAc6_OPS_HTTP_007_AC8_responseKeepsOnlyRedirectMarker changes its expectation from one marker line holding `res.redirect` to zero marker lines plus the post-v1 sentence; the AC8 methods requestKeepsNoMarker, expressKeepsOtherIssuesMarkers and routingKeepsNoMarker keep their expectations. Kept unchanged and not superseded: the defaults.md heading "저사양 Android 튜닝(수동 후속 작업)" (PERF-APP-001 AC-4, WaveSevenDocsTest), the three KEPT rows of AppDocsTest, the kept(...) rows of WaveFiveDocsTest, and the defaults.md "TLS 리스너" line (WaveFiveDocsTest:447). Rejected alternative: removing the three express markers and re-pointing the AppDocsTest, WaveFiveDocsTest and HttpDocsTest kept lists; the wave decision keeps the verified assertions and lists the three rows as open Express-compatibility items in the release notes.
